answer: Escrowed demand-comet: each identity must hold a small, time-decaying escrow that only refunds after its generated work is independently consumed downstream. Unused escrows forfeit into a canyon-shaped pool that funds challengers, so idle duplicates bleed value while real demand recovers it. An attacker opening N identities pays N escrows plus the decay slippage on unconsumed capacity, a linear cost per duplicate. Legitimate agents flow through this inlet at near-zero net cost since genuine coupling refunds fast.
